newsitem.title: INDIA: Death toll in India fire rises to 176 - police.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in India fire rises to 176 - police.

text.p: The death toll in a fire that swept through a gathering of Hindu worshippers in eastern India has risen to at least 176, and many more people were missing, authorities said on Monday.

Police in Baripada town, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital of Orissa state, Bhubaneshwar, said 154 devotees were burnt alive on Sunday when flames tore through bamboo and straw shelters. Another 22 died later in hospital, they said.

The raging blaze engulfed a cluster of shelters on the last day of a convention dedicated to a Hindu guru. All the victims were believed to be male. The cause of the fire was thought to be a short circuit or gas cylinder that exploded.
Officials at the camp ground, located on a football ground, said some 300 people from among the 15,000 who had attended the convention were missing.
News agencies said unofficial reports put the death toll at more than 250 people.

"The scene looked like people were roasted alive on a battlefield," said Amarendra Bose, a resident who visited the site after the fire. "The bodies were so mutilated that they were beyond recognition."
